#863. Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football

Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine

Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier.

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments.

“Of course, we plan to submit documents,” the Sevastopol CEO, Valery Chaly, told local media last month. “According to the regulations we should advance to the next stage.” The RFU remains a member of Uefa and Fifa but there would be fresh calls for it to be ejected if Sevastopol’s ascent is not blocked. It is understood no decision about their potential admission has been made.

Football’s governing bodies were given a similar dilemma in 2023 when Sevastopol and another Crimean club, Rubin Yalta, were accepted into FNL 2B even though sides from the occupied territory have not been allowed to compete in Russia since its annexation in 2014.

The Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) asked Uefa and Fifa to consider ejecting Russia, alleging a “gross violation” of their statutes and Uefa’s ruling, made in 2014, that Crimean clubs must not compete in RFU-run events. Uefa claimed it would assess the situation but the authorities appeared to turn a blind eye, the RFU saying it had created a workaround by making FNL 2B an amateur competition that it did not operate. At the time, several clubs at that level contacted by the Guardian confirmed informally that they were fully professional. No such blurring of the lines exists for FNL 2A, which has never denied its clubs are professional.

That unwillingness to act led to escalation when, in April 2024, an imitation of the Ukrainian club Zorya Luhansk – whose home city in Donbas is illegally occupied by Russia – was admitted to FNL 2B. This year they were joined by a fake Shakhtar Donetsk, mimicking the current Champions League side who have been forced to play elsewhere since 2014. Five of the 15 teams who completed the recent FNL 2B group one season played in or claimed to represent occupied areas, the Simferopol-based club Kyzyltash Bakhchisaray completing the quintet.

Should the RFS decide, of its own accord or under pressure from international bodies, to bar Sevastopol from promotion an even bigger flashpoint may await. The imitation Shakhtar finished runners-up in group 1, securing that spot by winning 2-0 at Sevastopol on the season’s final day last Saturday, and are next in line to go up. Unlike Sevastopol their home matches are played on Russian territory, in Taganrog, rather than an occupied area. The club is, however, registered to an address in Donetsk.

In October 2025 the UAF asked Uefa to review and explain the imitation clubs’ legal positions but, as with any assessment of the Crimean clubs’ participation, the results are still awaited. It warned of a“coordinated political attempt to legitimise the occupation and erase the identity of Ukrainian football”.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Last month Russia competed in a Fifa-run event for the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, finishing 19th in the new under-15 World Cup. Teams at under-15 and under-16 levels have continued to play in smaller Uefa development tournaments, largely against invited opponents on home soil, during the war in Ukraine.

None of Uefa, Fifa, the RFU, the FNL, Sevastopol or the imitation Shakhtar Donetsk offered comment when contacted by the Guardian.

#861. America Ferrera Reveals What She Knows About Barbie 2

As the deal for the sequel to Greta Gerwig’s Barbie movie up in the air, star America Ferrera revealed what she knows about the film in an exclusive E! News interview for The Cat in the Hat.

America Ferrera is a Barbie girl, but she knows nothing about the Barbie 2 world.

While the sequel for Greta Gerwig’s film inspired by the Mattel toy and starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling has been up in the air for years, Ferrera admitted that she’s just Ken, er, Gloria—and doesn’t have any update.

“I don’t know anything about Barbie 2,” Ferrera admitted in an exclusive E! News interview for The Cat in the Hat alongside costar Paula Pell. “I don’t have to pretend like I don’t know anything because I actually don’t know anything.”

Ferrera’s update comes as speculation swirls around the possibility for a follow-up to the 2023 film, with reports earlier this year noting that the movie could be shelved due to ongoing salary negotiations between Warner Bros. and the original film’s cast.

Meanwhile, Ferrera—mom to Sebastian, 8, and Lucia, 6, with husband Ryan Piers Williams—is excited about bringing another iconic character to life, starring as mom Carmen in the Bill Hader-led film.

“The Cat in the Hat is so iconic,” the Ugly Betty alum mused. “I grew up loving Dr. Seuss books and I have two littles and I’ve read The Cat in the Hat to them a ton. Actually, my favorite part of the book was always the very last line of the book which was, ‘What would you do if your mother asked you?’ And I’d always turn to my kids and be like, ‘Would you tell me the truth?’”

Fast forward to this opportunity, Ferrera admitted it felt as easy as counting one fish, two fish, red fish, blue fish to take the role.

“Getting to say to my kids I’m going to be the voice of the mom in The Cat in the Hat, I did it for them,” she mused. “But a little bit for me.”

And Ferrera’s kids already gave her a glowing review for the film, also starring Quinta Brunson and Bowen Yang, which officially hits theaters today, Nov. 6.

“We saw it yesterday,” she revealed. “We had the best time. They loved it. It was really sweet.”

Of course, Ferrera isn’t so sure her kids would, in fact, tell her if The Cat in the Hat came for a visit.

“I can’t tell if it gave me cool mom points or if they’re like, ‘Ugh, mom that’s you,’” she joked. “Because I am such a mom in this, too, where they were like, ‘We’ve heard the same things.’”

While Barbie 2 still remains uncertain, keep reading for secrets about the original film…

Margot Robbie, who stars as Barbie and also produced the film, admitted that she always wanted Ryan Gosling to be her Ken. She said he was written into the script—as the character "Ken Ryan Gosling"—and joked, "We pretty much wouldn't take no for an answer."

Writer-director Greta Gerwig had her back too. "We just kept bothering you," she said to to Ryan in an SXM interview. "Margot was like, 'Is it weird if I go to his house?' I was like, 'Don't go to his house. We're just gonna stay put.' Send a follow-up text."

As Margot teased, "I would see a sea of blue on my phone."

Margot gave Ryan daily gifts inspired by his character Beach Ken.

"She left a pink present with a pink bow, from Barbie to Ken, every day while we were filming," Ryan told Vogue. "They were all beach-related. Like puka shells, or a sign that says 'Pray for surf.'"

He said that he's "never quite figured out" what Ken's job as "Beach" means, "But I felt like she was trying to help Ken understand, through these gifts that she was giving."

"I think we said it was scheduling conflict, that's what we said," Amy Schumer said on Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen in June 2023. "But yeah, it really was just, like, creative differences. But you know what? There's, like, a new team behind it, and it looks like it's very feminist and cool. So, I will be seeing that movie."

These Barbies were almost movie stars—or, rather, these movie stars were almost Barbies. After Amy left the movie, Anne Hathaway was signed up to take the lead, but it was later reported that she was no longer involved. When Margot got on board, she tried to recruit Gal Gadot to join as another Barbie, but the Wonder Woman star wasn't available.

Greta's former Lady Bird and Little Women muse Saoirse Ronan was also set to appear in the film but had to cancel. "I was supposed to do a cameo because I live in London and they were [filming] there," the actress admitted to People. "There was a whole character I was going to play—another Barbie. I was gutted I couldn't do it."

"We've always tried to get in a proper fart joke and we've never done it," Greta told IndieWire. "We had like a fart opera in the middle [of Barbie]. I thought it was really funny... And that was not the consensus."

But her editor Nick Houy has hope she'll let one rip in a future film: "We need to work it into a more significant narrative moment next time."

While the script comedically name-drops other shows and movies—like the The Godfather, Pride and Prejudice and Zack Snyder's Justice League—there are multiple Easter eggs to The Wizard of Oz hidden in the set. A movie theater marquee shows that the 1939 film is playing in the doll world, but the inspiration didn't stop there.

"[The Wizard of Oz] does something that I wanted to emulate," Greta said in an interview, "which it's using these incredible sound stages and these painted skies and this sense of 'authentic artificial,' which I think is very beautiful and emotional."

The 39-year-old explained, "I think of the painted backdrop of the Emerald City as they go towards it, and we put in our movie, we have the pink brick road, instead of the yellow brick road. We also have beautiful painted backdrops of horizons. We executed it like they would have done in the ‘30s and ‘40s."

Spreading Christmas cheer in July, Will Ferrell made some cheeky nods to his beloved Elf character Buddy while playing the Mattel CEO in the Barbie movie.

Among the discreet references to the 2003 comedy? He demands to be the one to press a button in the Mattel office elevator (calling back to the Elf scene where he presses every button in his dad's office building elevator, because the lights look "like a Christmas tree").

In Barbie, his suited character also starts a tickle fight—just like Buddy the Elf does with his dad Walter (James Caan) while being tucked into bed one night.

Going where no Barbie has gone before... The opening scene of Barbie pays homage to the 1968 Stanley Kubrick film 2001: A Space Odyssey, which shows a group of hominins discovering a futuristic monolith. In Barbie, a group of girls are shocked by a giant version of the original 1959 Barbie doll, wearing a black and white striped swimsuit.

Fans speculate that Gloria's daughter Sasha (Ariana Greenblatt) and her friends in the cafeteria were inspired by Barbie's rivals, the original Bratz dolls: Sasha, Chloe, Yasmin and Jade.

Casting director Allison Jones revealed Saturday Night Live star Bowen Yang, Schitt's Creek actor Dan Levy and Dear Evan Hansen actor Ben Platt almost played Kens in the movie but weren't able to make it work. She added, "They were, I'm not kidding, really bummed they couldn't do it."

According to the casting director, before Michael Cera came on board as Ken's buddy Allan, the part almost went to a certain Frozen actor.

"Dear, dear Jonathan Groff was like, 'I can't believe I'm typing this,'" Allison told Vanity Fair, "'but I can't do Allan.'"

America Ferrera's IRL husband Ryan Piers Williams plays none other than her character Gloria's husband. Ryan—whose past work includes producing, writing and acting in X/Y with America in 2014—is credited as "El Esposo de Gloria."

"It was a happy accident," John Cena told Today of his casting as a Mermaid Ken. He said he "kind of" pitched himself to join the film "in an accidental run-in with Margot Robbie."

As he recalled, he told the actress, "'I would do, pretty much, whatever you guys need 'cause I really enjoy the movie,' and they asked me if I wanted to be a merman."

The French version of Barbie's poster went viral after social media users pointed out the double entendre of the translation. The tagline, "She can do everything. He's just Ken," was translated to, "Elle peut tout faire. Lui, c'est juste Ken."

However, fans went wild after pointing out that "ken" has a slang meaning in French as "f--k" and would translate to, "He can only f--k." Bonjour, Ken!

The Barbie actresses had a cast sleepover at London hotel Claridge's to get close. "We all shared beds and wore our pajamas, and ordered room service," Margot revealed on The Kelly Clarkson Show, "and played games, and found out that America is exceptionally competitive."

America had her own tea to spill about the evening. "Nobody told me that it was a sexy Barbie sleepover," she quipped. "So everybody was in like really pretty silky nightgowns, and I was in like the most grandma floral twin set you can imagine."

As for the Kens? "Greta was very deliberate in what she wanted the Kens to do to bond," Simu Liu exclusively told E! News, "which was to gym together."

Though Nicola Coughlan only appeared for a few moments in the film, it was very important to her that she experience life in plastic.

"I auditioned for Barbie back in January '22 when I was on holiday with friends," she wrote on Instagram. "I'd packed one random hot pink dress I hadn't worn at all and when I had to make my audition tape I thought—this is fate, I have a dress in Barbie Pink!"

Admitting she's "obsessed" with Greta, the Bridgerton star said that "the prospect of working with her was something I couldn't even have imagined."

"When I found out she wanted to have me be part of @barbiethemovie, and then that I probably wouldn't be able to make it work because of my schedule I was firstly elated and quickly heartbroken," Nicola continued. "So when I was asked if I wanted to pop into Barbieland even briefly my answer was an immediate, and very emphatic yes."

The film concludes with Margot adopting a new life as a human named Barbara Handler, a reference to Barbie inventor Ruth Handler's real-life daughter. Barbie enters an office building and delivers her final line to a receptionist: "I'm here to see my gynecologist."

Why did Greta end on that note? "With this film, it was important for me that everything operated on at least two levels," she told USA Today. "I knew I wanted to end on a mic drop kind of joke, but I also find it very emotional. When I was a teenage girl, I remember growing up and being embarrassed about my body, and just feeling ashamed in a way that I couldn't even describe. It felt like everything had to be hidden."

The director hoped the way Margot delivered the line with a "big old smile on her face" and with "such happiness and joy" would help de-stigmatize conversations about women's health and "give girls that feeling of, 'Barbie does it, too'—that's both funny and emotional."

#860. ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel

Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral

The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente.

The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said.

The club’s majority shareholder, Rayco García, had cried as they left the building where De Miguel’s body had laid in Santa Cruz de Tenerife and he asked the striker’s teammates to be close to his widow Maria, when he had vowed they would for ever take care of his daughter, Clara.

Maria was in the stands with 16-month-old Clara in her arms when, in the 96th minute of Monday’s second division game, she saw her partner chase a ball up the pitch to the centre circle where Owono crashed into him. De Miguel’s father was watching it from the hotel Alameda in Navahermosa, where he goes for most games. His son’s football career had mostly been played not far from there and from the Leganés home where he had grown up – at Fuenlabrada, Inter Madrid, Unión Adarve and Navalcarnero, then Salamanca and Castellón – but now he was 1,000 miles away.

Medical staff rushed on to the pitch. Players stood, terrified, while for six minutes De Miguel was treated there. He was then taken on a stretcher to the ambulance waiting in the corner where, the club reported, they were able to re-establish a pulse. He was transferred to the Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de Candelaria in Santa Cruz, where medics succeeded in getting him to breathe again. He remained in a critical condition but, with his body temperature lowered, he was stable, they said.

With De Miguel’s parents hurrying to find a flight to Santa Cruz, where García collected them, doctors told Tenerife there would be no news until the morning. But at 3am, there was another call to say his condition had deteriorated neurologically. At 8am, he passed away; Tenerife announced his passing at 8.31am. He was 30. The preliminary autopsy pointed to a trauma of the thorax: commotio cordis which can only occur upon impact within a 40-millisecond window in the cardiac cycle. A routine investigation was opened, the focus not just on Owono but the medical protocol applied.

Football is supposed to be a safe space, a refuge, an escape. All those lines about giving your life to the game are not supposed to be literal. This didn’t make sense. The images and the outcome shocked; the contradictory combination of the improbability and the plausibility of it all made it harder still to come to terms with: this couldn’t happen yet it could have happened to anyone. “I am the same age,” Raphinha, Barcelona’s captain, said. There is an everyman quality about De Miguel. He was also a partner, a father. “How we loved him,” García told Cadena Ser. “He was so humble, his feet on the ground.”

His teammate Javi Alonso said: “He was a worker, a footballing labourer. He was in the AFE, the players’ union, and helped me a lot. He was a great teammate and a good person, wonderful. He was always willing to help.”

He had begun in the academy at Leganés, a modest start to a career at modest clubs; real football. It hadn’t been easy and he had endured injuries too. He met Maria when he was playing for Navalcarnero in the third tier: she lived in one of the houses in front of the small, municipal ground with its astroturf pitch. It was not until he was 27 that he played “professionally”, always understood in Spain as referring to the first two divisions. He took his teams there too, twice winning promotion.

He never played in the top flight and played 40 games in the second division: he was not a star and was not rich. García vowed that his daughter would not want for anything. Fran Sol, a former Tenerife player, started a crowdfunding page for his family.

Almería said that their gate receipts when they play Tenerife would go to the family. During the funeral one of the eulogies noted that playing in segunda for Tenerife was his dream, finally fulfilled at 30: this wasn’t the end of his career; it was the start. When they won promotion, he told reporters: “When I started playing as a little kid, I never thought I would live all this.”

An interview he did with Ser Tenerife resurfaced this week in which he said: “Nothing in life is easy. There will be good moments and bad ones too; it is a path you have to walk. Making fans happy is what makes you proud; seeing people celebrate goals is the loveliest thing in football.”

Now they mourned him, desperately sad. Outside gate No 9 at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López, fans brought flowers and left candles. So too did the squad, standing in silence. The Spanish Federation cancelled all Copa del Rey games. The Champions League went ahead; Como’s Nico Paz, whose father played for Tenerife, held up a T-shirt in his honour. Messages came in from across the game; minutes’ silences were held. Las Palmas announced that they will wear their third kit this weekend, because it is blue and white, the same colour as their rivals’ shirt.

They would prefer not to play at all. The players’ union De Miguel was part of said it wanted to stop, that it had canvassed footballers and they agreed: they were not ready, their heads not right. But La Liga decided all games will go ahead except those involving Tenerife, Andorra and De Miguel’s former club Castellón – a decision they did not finally confirm until Thursday afternoon.

By then, De Miguel’s funeral had finished. His body was flown to the mainland on Wednesday, the decision made to hold the funeral in his parents’ village, although there will be an event at Tenerife’s stadium on Saturday, open to everyone. Tenerife’s players and staff boarded a charter at 7am on Thursday and then went to Navahermosa by bus, all of them. The presidents of the AFE, the federation and the league came; the presidents of Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid, too. Representatives from clubs across Spain. Andorra’s owner, Gerard Piqué; president, Ferran Vilaseca, and general manager, Jaume Nogués.

The minister of sport, Milagros Tolón Jaime. Pablo Blanco, ambassador of Sevilla, the club that lost Antonio Puerta and José Antonio Reyes. Their midfielder Giorgi Kochorashvili, a former teammate, who had asked for leave; the head coach, Luis García, said: “We’re people above all else.”

Before the cortege set off, Manuel Hernandez, De Miguel’s agent, said: “In those difficult moments, we want to thank everyone from the bottom of our hearts for the words and gestures, all the support we have received. We’re very grateful; to feel so much affection towards Jesús and see the impact he made on people is something we will always take with us. Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill but also leaves everyone who was fortunate enough to share their life with him great memories.”

Wreaths of flowers from all the clubs he had graced in his career covered the hearse as it edged towards the church, following the cross-bearer there, slowly and in silence. There was not enough room in the church for all those who were there. When they eventually came out on to the plaza again, Tenerife’s players lifted the coffin on to their shoulders and carried their teammate back through the crowd to his final resting place in Navahermosa.

#858. Kamada’s late leveller rescues point for 10-man Crystal Palace and denies Hoffenheim

A late, late strike from Daichi Kamada saved Crystal Palace from embarrassment and another round of navel gazing as they snatched a Europa League draw with Hoffenheim against the odds.

After being outplayed by a side currently in the bottom half of the Bundesliga, and a goal down from the seventh minute, Palace looked to have lost all hope in this fixture when Adam Wharton was dismissed with 13 minutes to go. But after Hoffenheim failed to clear a goalmouth scramble in added time, Kamada fired home under the keeper to generate a rare moment of elation at Selhurst Park this season.

After the match, the beleaguered Pierre Sage struggled to put a positive gloss on events. Asked if he thought his team had deserved their point, he said it “depended on the moment of the game”, and while he had praise for his side’s attitude he was critical of their tactical performance. “Offensively we did better than our two previous games but we have to continue to improve defensively”, he said. “We gave up too much space to the opponent and sometimes we had difficulty in duels. When we try to attack a little bit we are very quickly open.”

To be fair to Sage, this was an accurate call. Palace were in the match throughout without ever dominating, and Hoffenheim created the best chances in the game without ever having to try too hard. Sitting in 20th place in the Europa League, Palace have work to do in this competition, offering no respite from their Premier League travails as they prepare for a visit from Liverpool on Sunday.

With a tea-time kick-off on Bonfire Night, a family-friendly crowd might have had a right to expect fireworks. Palace set off with intensity but were sloppy too and coughed up an easy opening goal in the game’s early knockings. Wharton gave possession away cheaply about 20 yards from the Hoffenheim goal. There were perhaps just three touches before the ball reached Tim Lemperle wide right, who whipped the ball first time to the advancing Alexander Prass. The winger’s shot was equally immediate and caught Dean Henderson cold, his save too slow, and the ball squirmed through his midriff before rolling over the line.

The Palace support did not moan and got on with backing their side. Sadly the team on the pitch did not respond in desired fashion and Hoffenheim should have scored again through a Andrej Kramaric volley in the 23rd minute, well saved by Henderson on this occasion, before Palace started to work their way into the game.

Fabian Hürzeler saluted a professional performance from Brighton after they beat Getafe 1-0 in the Conference League.

Malick Yalcouyé scored his fourth goal of the season to break the deadlock in a hard-fought encounter in Madrid.

The Seagulls are now the only team not to have conceded a goal in the competition so far and their seven points from three matches leaves them fifth in the table.

“It’s what we expected,” said Hürzeler. “These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat the low block. We didn’t play our best game, to be fair. But in the end we kept a clean sheet – the fifth clean sheet in a row in this tournament – and then we scored the goal and I think we deserved to win this game.”

The Swiss side Lugano are top of the Conference League, with maximum points after a 3-0 win over Kauno Zalgiris at the AIL Arena.

Panathinaikos beat CSKA Sofia 2-1 to also make it three straight wins, Twente beat 10-man Pafos 3-1 and Monaco saw off Nordsjælland 2-0 to extend their own 100% start.

Ajax ran out 6-1 winners away to 10-man Midtjylland, while a depleted Hearts side lost 3-1 away to Thun in Switzerland.

Yéremy Pino was the focus of the home side’s hopes and he was both Palace’s brightest spark and their greatest frustration. He could find the gaps that no one else could but his delivery was either inaccurate or overcomplicated.

He did at least find the right weight on a through ball to Kamada on the half hour, only for his fellow No 10 in Sage’s system to pull a cross-shot beyond Oliver Baumann’s far post. Hoffenheim had a better opportunity for themselves just before half-time, Ozan Kabak heading over at a corner when unmarked six yards out.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The second half began with another burst of intensity from Palace but it fizzled out again and within 10 minutes Sage had made a double change, pulling Kamada back into midfield and bringing Eddie Nketiah into the front three to strengthen Palace’s finishing options. In the 66th minute Palace created their best chance of the match, when Wharton feigned to shoot from the edge of the box, cut left and slipped in Pino, who looked to shoot over the advancing Baumann only for the keeper to stand his ground and deflect the ball to safety.

You might have thought a rally could spring from there, but no. Hoffenheim soon won a couple of corners on the bounce and killed any momentum for the home side.

Then Wharton got himself sent off, making a poor decision to lead with his elbow in contesting a header. Horatiu Fesnic did not need a second look and despite Wharton’s protestations the referee showed him a second yellow card.

A sense of injustice did at least succeed in inducing some pep into Palace’s performance while Hoffenheim stepped back and sought to run down the clock. Palace created only one opportunity and that was a bit of a mess, but if there was to be respite from their perilous Premier League condition it was going to need a bit of fortune, and Kamada duly seized upon it when it arrived.

#857. England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or

The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time on Monday, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious football award since 2001.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker was honored at a ceremony at the London Palladium after scoring 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season.

The Ballon d'Or, awarded by French magazine France Football, is one of football's most prestigious individual honors, recognizing the world's best players.

The last English player to win the award was former Liverpool striker Michael Owen, who claimed the prize 25 years ago.

Kane's remarkable goalscoring record helped Bayern Munich secure a German league and cup double last season.

The former Tottenham Hotspur forward also led England to the World Cup semifinals, the country's best finish since winning the tournament in 1966.

Kane has finished as the Bundesliga's leading scorer for three consecutive seasons. He was also Europe's top club goalscorer during the 2025-26 campaign.

At Monday's ceremony, Kane thanked his Bayern Munich teammates for their support.

"Without you guys (his Bayern Munich team-mates) and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much," he said.

Kane also paid tribute to his former club Tottenham Hotspur, which he joined at the age of 11, as well as his England teammates and family.

"To my wife Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs. You are my biggest support and I felt like you wanted this more than me," he said.

Reflecting on his career, Kane encouraged young footballers to pursue their ambitions despite setbacks.

"I hope my journey, it wasn't straightforward, I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now. I hope that can give you inspiration."

Kane faced strong competition from Barcelona's Spanish teenager Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's French forward Kylian Mbappe.

He joins Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen among the English players to have won the award.

Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas claimed the women's Ballon d'Or for the third time in her career, having previously won the award in 2021 and 2022.

The 32-year-old was recognized after a successful season with Barcelona, winning the treble and scoring 21 goals across all competitions.

Putellas also played a key role in Barcelona's Champions League triumph, contributing seven goals and seven assists during the campaign.

She joined English club London City Lionesses in July after spending 14 years at Barcelona.

Her victory ended a run of three consecutive Ballon d'Or wins by fellow Spaniard Aitana Bonmatí.

Barcelona's Lamine Yamal won the Kopa Trophy for the best young male player for the third consecutive year, while his teammate Vicky Lopez claimed the women's award for the second year running.

Barcelona coach Pere Romeu was named women's coach of the year, while Spain manager Luis de la Fuente won the men's coaching award.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon received the men's Yashin Trophy, with Cata Coll winning the women's equivalent.

Barcelona was named women's club of the year, while Paris Saint-Germain took the men's award.

#855. Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words

The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff

Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon.

“It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.”

Parker is back in the thick of it. Out of work after leaving Burnley in the wake of relegation from the Premier League last April, he cut short his break from management when West Ham parted company with Nuno Espírito Santo. Nuno was sacked early on Tuesday and replaced by Parker, who is intent on leading West Ham out of the Championship at the first time of asking.

It will not be easy. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after three games without a win and displayed their inconsistencies against Cardiff. They made another slow start, conceding three during the first half, but roared back after a triple half-time change from Parker. Jarrod Bowen was inspired. But Parker needs complete performances if West Ham are to win automatic promotion.

“The Championship’s a tough league,” he said. “It doesn’t matter what name you have on a bit of paper. You have to have a level of humility of what this league needs. That’s a challenge when you come out of the Premier League.”

Parker argued that talent was not enough. Burnley were stingy when they won promotion. Parker has to sort out West Ham’s defence. “Of course we want to play a certain brand,” the 46-year-old said. “But I think it’s just a non-negotiable in terms of a committed team.”

Connections need to be rebuilt with disillusioned supporters. Parker was an all-action midfielder who loved his four years at West Ham as a player. He has added Mark Noble to his backroom staff. Noble has held the role of West Ham’s sporting director since retiring in 2022 but Parker confirmed the former club captain would have a role as an assistant coach. “He’s going to be coaching with me and be that sounding board,” Parker said.

Noble will be able to get Parker up to speed on his squad. West Ham need improvement at the back, better balance in midfield and more bite up front. Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, could be busy in January. Parker wants to give everyone a clean slate, though. Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez will have opportunities. Even Maxwel Cornet travelled with the squad to Cardiff.

Parker did not focus during negotiations with Karim Virani, West Ham’s interim CEO, and Daniel Kretinsky, the club’s largest shareholder, on whether funds would be available for signings. One step at a time.

West Ham are in transition. David Sullivan still owns a 40% stake but is no longer on the board. Kretinsky’s power has grown, although the Czech billionaire is yet to say much in public. Parker has heard more from Kretinsky than most people.

“I found a man that was hugely passionate,” Parker said. “I instantly felt that, along with Karim, along with Nils. These were three people who know where they want the club to go.”

The target is a return to the top flight. Parker has won promotion with Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham but his record at keeping teams up is less impressive. He has been dismissed a little unfairly as nothing more than a promotion specialist.

“In a short space of a coaching career I’ve had some huge success,” Parker said. “I’ve had some blips in terms of two full seasons in the Premier League. All I know is that I’m fully committed.”

That mindset convinced Kretinsky, Virani and Koppen to pick Parker. They wanted his knowledge of the club and record at this level.

West Ham are eighth before visiting Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. They are taking 7,000 fans to Ewood Park and Parker knows there can be no more complacency.

#854. A Stranger Things Prequel Is Coming: What to Know About Other Worlds

More Stranger Things is officially on the way, Netflix having announced a prequel series titled Other Worlds is in the works: “There are so many more mysteries to explore.”

It’s why, as a friend, we’d never lie about the fact that another Stranger Things series is headed your way. And this time, the clocks are being wound all the way back to the 1950s.

Get ready to sock hop your way back a few decades with Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure. Netflix announced the live action prequel series on Nov. 6, confirming Matt Duffer and Ross Duffer will remain at the helm of the franchise along with the series’ longtime writer, showrunner and co-creator Katie Tefry.

Other Worlds predates even the events of the stage play Stranger Things: The First Shadow, which chronicles a teenaged Henry Creel’s path from a high school outcast to the evil Vecna.

For the Duffer Brothers, they were more than ready to run back up that hill and into the Upside Down.

“We’ve been dreaming of Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure for many years now, and to see it become a reality is surreal and exhilarating,” they said in the announcement. “It’s Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new … actually, we’re not allowed to say any more.”

And as they set their sights on casting the series, they added, “In the meantime—watch the skies, nerds!”

But for anyone who are desperate for the exact details of the series, searching for additional meaning in the tidbits of information shared might prove to be as hard as interpreting flickering Christmas lights. (Maybe ask Joyce Byers for help.)

After all, Tefry only teased, “We have had the time of our lives returning to all the horror, wonder and mystery of the flagship, while also telling a wholly new story, one we hope will blow your minds and break your hearts all over again. There are so many more mysteries to explore.”

Executive producer and director Shawn Levy, meanwhile, hinted that the series is aptly named, likely taking viewers far beyond the Midwest setting of the original series.

“With Other Worlds, the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry craft a new ensemble and adventure that is imbued with the DNA of our flagship series,” he shared, “while exploring a new era, setting, and all-new characters, themes, and mythology—the seeds of which may have been planted in Hawkins, but now venture into other worlds of spectacle, action, and emotion.”

After all, the door was still kept open three inches at the end of Stranger Things, allowing for more stories and history to slip through the crack.

However, and don’t call us a mouthbreather for saying it, but it will likely take a long time for Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure to hit screens.

In the meantime, read on to relive all the b--chin’ secrets behind the original series.

1. After working on M. Night Shyamalan's Fox series Wayward Pines, brother writing duo Matt Duffer and Ross Duffer came up with the concept for Stranger Things, though it was initially called Montauk.

"It's very hard when your brain is latched onto a title, it's really, really hard to get people to agree and accept another title," Matt told The Daily Beast in 2016. "Initially when we came up with this title Stranger Things, it was hard for people to embrace."

2. The Duffers envisioned filming the series on Long Island, but it ultimately proved to be too challenging.

"We liked Montauk, because we liked the coastal setting, and Montauk was the basis for Amity, and Jaws is probably our favorite movie, so I thought that that would be really cool," Matt explained to The Hollywood Reporter. "Then it was really going to be impossible to shoot in or around Long Island in the wintertime. It was just going to be miserable and expensive."

Atlanta ultimately became the home base for production.

3. Before Netflix picked up the series, almost 20 networks passed on the project, according to Vulture, with executives believing audiences would not be able to invest in a show starring four children.

4. To play Eleven, then 12-year-old Millie Bobby Brown had to say goodbye to her hair.

"The day I shaved my head was the most empowering moment of my whole life," the actress reflected during PaleyFest in 2018. "The last strand of hair cut off was the moment my whole face was on show and I couldn't hide behind my hair like I used to. As I looked in the mirror I realized I had one job to do: inspire...You don't need hair to be beautiful."

5. She drew inspiration from Charlize Theron in Mad Max: Fury Road, as well as costar Winona Ryder's old yearbook photos.

"Winona looked cool back in the day with the pixie cut," she shared, "and I thought maybe I could bring it back!"

6. The British actress revealed she turned to a surprising source to perfect her American accent: Miley Cyrus' Hannah Montana. "It's so good," she told Jimmy Fallon during a visit to The Tonight Show. "Like the film, everything. Everything about it is amazing. And I got the American accent."

7. To find their four main kids, the Duffer brothers had the young actors audition with scenes from Stand By Me.

8. When it came to finding their Mike, the brothers had a different idea for the character. That is, until Finn Wolfhard auditioned.

"Originally Mike was a sigher, he was a dreamer, he was much more like Mikey in The Goonies in a lot of ways," Matt told The Daily Beast in 2016. "But Finn had this really anxious, twitchy energy about him and we thought that that was really great and we just kind of wrote the character to match him and his personality."

9. Another actor who influenced his character was Gaten Matarazzo as Dustin. As Matt explained, "I don't think we really understood who that character was. He started out more like a stereotypical nerd and then we met Gaten and we basically tailored the show to him."

10.Thanks to Eleven's affinity for Eggo waffles, Kellogg's saw a significant increase in sales after the show. The company said consumption was up 14 percent in late 2017 after season two was released and October saw the most mentions of the product on social media in a single month.

11. In early 2018, David Harbour went viral after he fulfilled a fan's request to take her senior portraits with her after. She tweeted, "How many retweets for you take my senior photos with me," to which he replied, "25k. And I get to wear the school sweatshirt and hold a trombone." The actor held true to his word.

As he wrote on Instagram at the time. "Voted most likely to hijack someone's high school senior photos 24 years later."

12. Later that year, Harbour was once again up to his social media shenanigans, this time officiating a viewer's wedding in exchange for 125,000 retweets and the first slice of cake. He got ordained and performed her marriage ceremony dressed as Chief Hopper.

13. Many fans theorized that Eleven could be Hopper's daughter, though he eventually became her surrogate father. And in a sweet Easter egg, Eleven was seen wearing the blue braided bracelet Hopper always wore, made from his late daughter's hair ribbon, at her school dance in the season two finale.

14. Eleven's season one kiss with Mike was Millie's first kiss ever. "It was a strange experience," she admitted, "Having 250 people looking at you kissing someone is like, 'Whoa!'"

15. And when the pair had to smooch again the following season, she revealed what her costar whispered in her ear.

"He wanted to let me know he was, like, kissing me then," she explained during a 2017 appearance on The Tonight Show. "So he was like, 'I'm coming in,' and he was like a ventriloquist! It was the craziest thing."

16. Natalia Dyer and Charlie Heaton, who play love interests Nancy and Jonathan, began dating in 2016, but have mostly kept their relationship private.

"That's something important to me—with my family, with my friends, I really like to keep it for me," Natalia told Refinery 29, though she did admit, "It's an interesting thing to work with somebody who you go home with. It's always really fun."

17. Believe it or not, Joe Keery's well-coiffed Steve Harrington was not supposed to make it out of season one alive.

But, "we fell in love with him during the making of season one, which is why we ended up writing that arc for him where he's helping to save the day with Jonathan and Nancy," Ross told The Hollywood Reporter. "Steve was supposed to be this jocky douchebag, and Joe was so much more than that."

18. Also slated to perish was Eleven. Yes, really.

"Eleven was going to sacrifice herself to save the day," Ross said in the 2018 book Stranger Things: Worlds Turned Upside Down. "That was always the end game. But once we realized that the show was potentially going to go on longer than one season, we needed to leave it more up in the air, because deep down we knew the show just wouldn't really work without Eleven. And at that point, we knew how special Millie was. If there was going to be more Stranger Things, Eleven had to come back."

19. The seventh episode of season two—titled "The Lost Sister"—almost never made it to air, with the Duffer brothers telling Vulture they were concerned the outing, which centers on Eleven going off to find another child who was experimented on, would break up the story's pacing.

"When we got to the point of writing the episode, we wanted to see if we really needed it or not," Matt explained. "We actually did toy with pulling the episode completely, but then the ending with Eleven didn't work at all. It just didn't land at all. Then we ended up deciding we needed it."

20. Eleven's sibling was written to be a boy, with the episode originally titled "The Lost Brother."

But after the audition was opened up to all young actors, it was Linnea Berthelsen who landed the part, and the episode ultimately featured Eleven meeting her "sister" Kali."Linnea and Millie really had a connection," Matt said, "Millie was like, 'I want to do this with Linnea.'"

21. Bridgerton actress Nicola Coughlan initially auditioned for the role of Robin before booking the role of Penelope Featherington years later. Maya Hawke ultimately nabbed the part, with Nicola saying Hawke was "was far better than I ever would have been."

She added, "It's a good lesson to actors: Watch the stuff you didn't get, because you'll totally understand how it's not personal. You're just right for some things and you're not right for other things."

22. Before playing Sarah on Netflix's Outer Banks, Madelyn Cline appeared in season two as Hawkins High school mean girl Tina.

23. To win the part of Billy, the mullet-rocking bad boy older stepbrother of Max (Sadie Sink), Australian actor Dacre Montgomery filmed a fun, yet slightly raunchy, audition tape, telling GQ he "wanted to make a bit of a splash with the Duffers."

That meant filming himself dancing to classic 1980s songs like "Come on Eileen" and "Hungry Like the Wolf" in nothing but a G-string. Dacre admitted he had some hesitation about sending it, saying, "Either I'm never going to work again, or somebody somewhere is going to see one thing in me, and they'll give me a chance." Fortunately, his risk paid off.

24. Heading into season three, Deadline reported that the cast received major pay increases, with the younger cast going from about $30,000 per episode to more than $200,000 per episode, and possibly even $250,000. Winona and David, meanwhile, were reportedly taking home about $300,000 to $350,000 per episode, while Natalia and Charlie were making $100,000 to $150,000 per episode.

25. While Priah Ferguson was intended to only appear in one episode in season two as Erica, Lucas' sassy little sister, the Duffer brothers kept finding ways to add the scene-stealer. She was made a series regular the following season.

26. Given that the younger cast was still growing as the series was filming, the wardrobe department faced a unique challenge when it came to continuity.

"It's crazy," costume designer Kim Wilcox told E! News. "We had one kid we could not keep in shoes, like every three weeks he grew a half-size." Her solution was to find heritage brands that make the same product in multiple sizes. "We'd buy five of them so that when somebody grew we'd have something."

27. While the Duffers were paying homage The Goonies, E.T., and Stand By Me, they were cautious not to be too overt in their references.

"When we billed the project to Netflix, we had this big two-and-a-half-minute trailer that had about 20 or 30 of these movies kind of woven together to try and tell the story of Stranger Things, but obviously all these images or ideas were in our heads," Matt told The Daily Beast. "Those are the movies that we grew up on and they're so much a part of our DNA. But then when you get into the writers' room and you're working on individual episodes, actually very little time is spent referencing other movies. Mostly you're just trying to tell the story, letting the characters guide where everything's going. Otherwise it would just be a jumble and a mess."

28. The creative team set out to use as little special effects as possible to achieve a throwback feel, but quickly learned how difficult that would be.

"The funny thing is that the original goal was to do entirely practical effects. But what we realized—and it really made us admire those guys who did The Thing and Alien and whatever—is that doing practical is really hard," Ross explained. "It takes a lot of time and preparation. We were turning out scripts as quickly as we could but they don't have six months to prep this stuff. You show up on set and stuff that seemed like it would be a great idea to do in that old school way, we didn't have time to do."

29. When they first pitched the show, the Duffers always envisioned a five-season arc. "So much of what they had in their head in 2015 is what we're now seeing play out as we come to the end of this series," Netflix executive Matthew Thunell told Variety, with the magazine reporting that each of season four's episodes cost $30 million.

30. While an ending for Stranger Things has been set, the Duffer brothers aren't ready to leave the Upside Down just yet.

"We do have an idea for a spin-off that we're super excited about," they said in an email interview with Variety, "but we haven't told anyone the idea yet, much less written it."Despite their efforts to keep it a surprise, Matt and Ross admitted that Finn already guessed the premise of the series, which they described as "very, very different." They added, "Aside from Finn, no one else knows!"

#853. Forest need balance between Woodstock and military - Glasner

Nottingham Forest's defeat at Brentford was their sixth defeat in 10 games in all competitions this season

Oliver Glasner insists his struggling Nottingham Forest side cannot survive on "flower power" as he tries to find a combination of trust and respect from his squad.

Forest are 19th in the Premier League and winless and goalless at home in the top flight.

Last weekend's 2-0 defeat at Brentford was a fourth defeat in five games as Glasner warned there would be no more compromises after his summer arrival, and he has underlined his standards.

"These are my two values I will never negotiate about, this is trust and respect," he said.

"It can't be one, so if it's just respect, I would say that's military. Then, after a few months of the national service, you are pleased when you can leave."

Glasner drew comparisons with the Woodstock music festival in the 1960s.

"When it's just trust, it's a flower power, just flying," he said. "Everybody can do what he wants and it's nice and great - Woodstock - but it's not high-performance Woodstock.

"Military is [high performance], to be honest, because otherwise this huge organisation couldn't work, and I felt we had too much Woodstock.

"We need a good balance between Woodstock, having fun, but also military, high performance. That's the most important thing, high performance, because that's what we get paid for, that's our job. If we have this - fly."

When asked by BBC Sport if he should have told his players sooner Glasner said: "I always ask myself this question - should I have done it earlier?

"Of course, maybe two or three times I felt it's time and then I thought 'no, come on Oliver, be patient and maybe things change'.

"Then it seemed to be the same game [Brentford] like the last ones, so I felt I have to say it now because otherwise things won't change."

Glasner is not under immediate pressure and remains in close communication with the Forest hierarchy, with stability desired after four managers last season.

The 52-year-old has made a positive impression with his work and methods, even if there have been some obvious grumbles from players who are not playing, and there remains a desire to stay calm.

"I'm always in contact with the ownership," Glasner said. "It's not always Mr [Evangelos] Marinakis because he has other stuff to do, but there is his son [Miltiadis], George [Syrianos, chief football officer] and Pedro [Ferreira, technical director] here at the training ground, and Theodore [Giannikos] the CEO.

"There's always communication - and that's a good thing, because everybody understands better why I am how I am. I never say what's best for Oliver Glasner, because I don't feel important. I will always say what I believe is best for Nottingham Forest, for the club.

"I don't like to accept things if I feel they are wrong. My addiction is to succeed with Nottingham Forest and, right now, I have failed. Then I get really upset with myself because I want to meet the expectations of the players, owner and the fans.

"Right now, I've failed and that's why I blame myself most."

#852. Europa League: Sunderland lose at home to Zagreb while Celtic enjoy first win

Evanilson helps Bournemouth to 3-1 win at Sparta Prague

Ferencvaros prevail 2-0 at Milan to keep 100% record

Sunderland’s unbeaten run in the Europa League came to an end as they were beaten 2-0 by Dinamo Zagreb at the Stadium of Light.

Dinamo went ahead through Luka Stojkovic’s fierce strike and the midfielder turned provider for Dion Drena Beljo to double their advantage before the break.

Sunderland had opportunities to get back into it as Wilson Isidor’s header was chalked off for offside two minutes after the restart and Kevin Danso hit the crossbar before Brian Brobbey went close.

However, Régis Le Bris’ side ultimately fell to their first defeat in four Europa League matches to continue a worrying run of form, with the club bottom of the Premier League.

Substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Durán sparked Celtic into life as the Scottish champions got off the mark in the Europa League in a 3-2 victory over Besiktas.

Martin O’Neill’s side were heading for a seventh defeat in 11 matches and bottom place when Junior Olaitan netted on the rebound after Sam Johnstone had saved his 54th-minute penalty.

But Osmand drilled home the equaliser with his first touch in the 62nd minute, seconds after coming off the bench in a triple change, and the 20-year-old set up Durán to put the hosts in front.

Besiktas substitute Orkun Kokcu equalised from long range but Celtic went back in front within 60 seconds when Durán stabbed home an 87th-minute winner from six yards.

The win hands Celtic a fighting chance of progressing especially with Portuguese second-tier side Torreense as their next opponents.

Bournemouth extended their winning run to seven matches as Evanilson’s wonderful late goal helped earn a 3-1 win away to 10-man Sparta Prague in the Europa League.

Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a dream start to the club’s debut European season and they will be confident of securing direct passage to the last 16 after making it four victories from four, but they were made to work hard for the points in the Czech capital.

They went behind in the first half to a piece of individual brilliance by Gambian forward Ebrima Singhateh, minutes after Lewis Cook had spurned the chance to give them the lead when his penalty struck a post. But Tobias Guddal let his team down badly when he picked up a second yellow card within two minutes of his side taking the lead.

Bournemouth had not conceded a goal on their six-game winning streak and they responded to the setback of falling behind by punishing Guddal’s error, levelling in the 57th minute when Tyler Adams smashed a loose ball into the bottom corner.

From then on there looked like being only one winner. Evanilson’s 81st-minute effort, finished low across the goalkeeper, put them in front before Rayan added gloss with a third at the death.

Fabian Hürzeler saluted a professional performance from Brighton after they beat Getafe 1-0 in the Conference League.

Malick Yalcouyé scored his fourth goal of the season to break the deadlock in a hard-fought encounter in Madrid.

The Seagulls are now the only team not to have conceded a goal in the competition so far and their seven points from three matches leaves them fifth in the table.

“It’s what we expected,” said Hürzeler. “These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat the low block. We didn’t play our best game, to be fair. But in the end we kept a clean sheet – the fifth clean sheet in a row in this tournament – and then we scored the goal and I think we deserved to win this game.”

The Swiss side Lugano are top of the Conference League, with maximum points after a 3-0 win over Kauno Zalgiris at the AIL Arena.

Panathinaikos beat CSKA Sofia 2-1 to also make it three straight wins, Twente beat 10-man Pafos 3-1 and Monaco saw off Nordsjælland 2-0 to extend their own 100% start.

Ajax ran out 6-1 winners away to 10-man Midtjylland, while a depleted Hearts side lost 3-1 away to Thun in Switzerland.

Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100% record in Europe.

Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.

Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting in this competition, just as we do in the others,” Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim, said.

In Germany, Marseille earned their first three points of the competition thanks to a stunning solo effort from Amine Gouiri after a largely uneventful contest against Bayer Leverkusen. The forward broke the deadlock in the 77th minute, collecting the ball near halfway before ‌surging past defenders and firing a right-footed shot into the net.

Juventus prevailed 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar, with Teun Koopmeiners opening the scoring against a team captained by his brother Peer in the 19th minute. The ​Dutch midfielder swept home a first-time finish after Randal Kolo Muani beat his marker down the right and cut the ball back to the edge of the area.

Kolo Muani doubled Juventus’s lead eight minutes before half-time, punishing an error forced by the visitors’ high press before cutting inside and drilling a low shot into the far corner. Mexx Meerdink pulled one back late on but AZ ⁠could not find an equaliser.

Juventus are fifth, level on 10 points with Union Saint Gilloise ​and Olympiacos.

#851. 'A void that is impossible to fill' - tributes paid at De Miguel funeral

Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in the town of Navahermosa in Spain on Thursday

Jesus de Miguel's family said "the mark he has left on so many people" was something they would always remember as the footballer's funeral took place on Thursday.

The Tenerife forward, who was 30, died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

After colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch while being treated by medical staff and was taken to hospital, where he died at 07:00 GMT on Tuesday.

Owono was sent off for the challenge and the game was abandoned.

De Miguel's funeral was held in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo, about 125km from the Spanish capital Madrid.

His Tenerife team-mates carried his coffin before the service at San Miguel Arcangel.

Current Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was among the mourners, along with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin and former Real and Spain coach Jose Antonio Camacho.

De Miguel's agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of the family, which read: "Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us.

"We cannot find enough words to thank you for every message, every phone call and every gesture of affection we are receiving.

"Feeling such affection for Jesus and seeing the mark he has left on so many people is something we will always carry with us.

"Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill, but also cherished memories for all of us who were fortunate enough to share our lives with him."

Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel, who joined Tenerife in the summer of 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competitions this week.

In a statement issued by his club Andorra on Wednesday, goalkeeper Owono said he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life".

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus," he added. "I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."

In the hours after the death was announced, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez - the stadium on the island of Tenerife, where Monday's game took place.

"We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation demands," the statement added.

"We appreciate the affection, concern and expressions of support that his loss is inspiring, and we are deeply grateful to you all."

Spain coach and Real Madrid president attend De Miguel funeral

The Spanish footballers' union, the AFE, made a request on Thursday for all this weekend's matches to be postponed out of respect for De Miguel.

Tenerife's match at Granada and Andorra's game against Mallorca have already been postponed, as were several midweek cup fixtures.

However, all Spanish sides in European competition have played their games this week.

The AFE said of the weekend games: "The footballers have expressed their deep sorrow for this loss and do not believe that there are the psychological and humane conditions necessary for the competition to be played in normal circumstances."

The union said its members "in every category" believed "unanimously" that the matches should not be played.

#850. Cape Verde captain Ryan Mendes cleared of rape allegation as woman charged with false statement

New Zealand police dismiss claim of sexual assault at Auckland hotel

Incident alleged to have occurred after football friendly in March

New Zealand police have dismissed a rape allegation against Cape Verde football captain Ryan Mendes and have charged the accuser with making a false statement.

Detective inspector Scott Beard said Friday the claim that a sexual assault occurred at a central Auckland hotel in March had not been substantiated.

A 40-year-old woman has been charged under New Zealand’s Crimes Act with making a false statement. She is expected to appear in court next week.

“A decision to prosecute in these circumstances is not taken lightly and follows months of investigative work by our Adult Sexual Assault Team,” Beard said.

The incident was alleged to have occurred hours after Cape Verde played Chile in a friendly match in Auckland, won 4-2 by Chile.

Mendes’ lawyer, Karl Trotter, said the allegation resulted in his client facing intense international media speculation.

Cape Verde qualified for the 2026 World Cup and the subject of the alleged assault arose at almost every media conference Mendes attended.

“Mr Mendes was thrilled to finally be able to get this behind him and he regards it as a complete vindication,” Karl Trotter told the New Zealand Herald newspaper.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

“It is to be hoped that this recent turn of events, clearing Mr Mendes of the allegation of rape, attracts the same level of media attention as the original reporting.”

The 36-year-old Mendes is Cape Verde’s most capped player, having made 103 appearances since his debut in 2010. He currently plays for RS Berkane in Morocco.

#849. Ronaldo's most iconic moments as he retires from international football

Cristiano Ronaldo became the first player to win five Champions League trophies and remains the top scorer in the tournament's history

Cristiano Ronaldo says his international career with Portugal is over, meaning the 41-year-old will just play on with Al-Nassr.

The main thing driving him on now is hoping to reach an unprecedented 1,000 career goals - he is currently on 985.

BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of a career that has also taken in spells at Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory

Ronaldo will not retire until he scores 1,000 goals

Untouchable or a support act? Ronaldo's 1,000-goal quest continues

Cristiano Ronaldo had one season in the Sporting first team before moving to Old Trafford

After 31 first-team games and five goals for Sporting, Ronaldo caught the eye of Manchester United in a pre-season friendly in 2003, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win in Lisbon.

Ronaldo revealed that United boss Alex Ferguson took him into the dressing room afterwards to meet the players.

Five days later he joined the Red Devils for Â£12m.

"After we played Sporting the lads in the dressing room talked about him constantly, and on the plane back from the game they urged me to sign him - that's how highly they rated him," said Ferguson.

"He is one of the most exciting young players I've ever seen."

Cristiano Ronaldo has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia

Ronaldo won the FA Cup in his first season at United, scoring in the final against Millwall.

But it was in 2006-07 that his career really exploded. He hit 17 Premier League goals, his first season of double figures, was named player of the year and young player of the year - and won his first league title.

The following season was even better, winning his first Champions League - scoring in the final - his first European Golden Shoe for top scorer, and another league title.

Cristiano Ronaldo won the first Puskas award - and it remains the only Champions League goal to win it

Ronaldo scored 118 goals in 292 games in his first spell at United, and one was ranked above all the others.

He hit an absolute rocket of a shot into the top corner from 40 yards in his homeland against Porto, a goal which took them into the Champions League semi-finals.

It won the inaugural Fifa Puskas award for goal of the year.

Months later, Ronaldo joined Real Madrid for Â£80m.

Cristiano Ronaldo helped Real Madrid to win their first Copa del Rey in seven years

Ronaldo's first season at Real Madrid produced no trophies and his second saw just the Copa del Rey won.

That final was especially notable because it is the first time Ronaldo had scored the winning goal in a final. And it was in El Clasico, one of four meetings in 18 days in all competitions.

He rose at the far post to power in a trademark header from Angel di Maria's cross in extra time as Real beat Barcelona 1-0.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored 14 goals in 14 games against Levante

Ronaldo, then 30, scored in a 3-0 La Liga win over Levante in October 2015 to become the club's all-time top scorer with his 324th goal in 310 games.

The 2015-16 campaign would go on to be the sixth season in a row that Ronaldo scored 50 or more goals in all competitions.

Ronaldo ended up extending that record by 126 goals - leaving Real with 450 goals in just 438 games.

Cristiano Ronaldo is the top scorer in European Championship history - with 14 goals - as well as lifting the trophy once

The one thing missing from Ronaldo's CV was international success.

And that came in 2016 when Portugal won the European Championship by beating hosts France 1-0 in the final in Paris.

Ronaldo ended up taking on an unofficial coaching role in that final after going off injured in tears midway through the first half.

He was named in the team of the tournament after three goals and three assists. Ronaldo retires as the top scorer in Euros history, with 14 goals.

Cristiano Ronaldo has won five Ballons d'Or, only behind Lionel Messi

Cristiano Ronaldo won his fifth Ballon d'Or, equalling Lionel Messi's record at the time, after winning the Champions League and La Liga in 2016-17. He netted twice in that European final over Juventus.

It followed on from the best player in the world awards in 2008, 2013, 2014 and 2016.

Sadly for Ronaldo, Messi would go on to win three more Ballons d'Or, meaning he won their personal rivalry 8-5.

Cristiano Ronaldo scored one of his eight Champions League hat-tricks in the 2017 win over Bayern Munich

Ronaldo became the first player to score 100 Champions League goals with a hat-trick in the 2016-17 quarter-final second leg win over Bayern Munich.

Only Messi and Robert Lewandowski have joined him to date in the century club.

Ronaldo would go on to score 141 goals in 187 games (also a record) in Europe's top competition. For six seasons in a row he was the tournament's top scorer or joint top scorer.

"That is one of the great goals you will seeâ¦ I was going to say Champions League football, but, basically, football," said Pat Nevin in BBC Radio 5 Live commentary

In 2018 came one of the most iconic moments of Ronaldo's career, maybe the greatest Champions League goal ever scored.

In the quarter-final, Ronaldo leapt into the air before acrobatically firing into the corner of the net with an incredible bicycle kick against Juventus.

Even the Juve fans stood up to applaud the player who would join their club months later.

It was nominated for the Puskas Award but he finished second to Mohamed Salah's goal for Liverpool against Everton.

The night Juventus rose to applaud Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first man to win five Champions Leagues, although he was not the last as Real Madrid kept winning it without him

Ronaldo won two La Liga titles and two Copa del Rey trophies at Real Madrid, but it was in Europe's elite club competition where he became a true legend.

He had already won the Champions League in 2008 with United, and went on to win it four more times with Real.

The first was in 2014 before a remarkable three times in a row in 2016, 2017 and 2018 (beating Liverpool in the Gareth Bale/Loris Karius final) to become the first player to win the Champions League five times.

Since his departure, former Real team-mates Toni Kroos, Dani Carvajal, Luka Modric and Nacho have gone on to win six.

Cristiano Ronaldo had a penalty saved by Gavin Bazunu before netting twice to deny Ireland a famous win in Faro

Ali Daei scored 109 goals for Iran between 1993 and 2006 - and it was felt like maybe his world record for international goals in men's football would never be broken.

But Ronaldo's two late headers in a World Cup qualifying win over the Republic of Ireland in 2021 took him onto 111 goals.

He kept adding to that total and finished on 146 goals in 234 caps - also a record for international appearances.

Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player in professional football to ever hit 900 official goals

Ronaldo continued to smash the goals in for Juventus, in his second spell at United and at Al-Nassr but failed to really replicate many truly magic moments of the past.

However he did create some history in 2024 as he became the first player to score 900 top-level career goals as Portugal beat Croatia.

That number is now 985 - so he is only 15 off an unprecedented 1,000th goal.

He has now hit five for Sporting, 450 for Real Madrid, 145 for Manchester United, 101 for Juventus, 138 for Al-Nassr and 146 for Portugal.

He recently confirmed that he is aiming to hit the 1,000 mark.

But old rival Messi is on 931 goals, the second highest scorer ever, so Ronaldo cannot afford to dawdle too much...
